Certificate (complexity).fact: In computational complexity theory, a certificate (also called a witness) is a string that certifies the answer to a computation, or certifies the membership of some string in a language. Certificate revocation list.subject: Computer & IT
Certificate revocation list.question: The _____ was List of revoked digital certificates.
Certificate revocation list.fact: In cryptography, a certificate revocation list (CRL) is "a list of digital certificates that have been revoked by the issuing certificate authority (CA) before their scheduled expiration date and should no longer be trusted".

Certificate revocation list.subject: Computer & IT
Certificate revocation list.question: Publicly trusted CAs in the Web PKI are required (including by the CA/_____ forum) to issue CRLs for their certificates, and they widely do
Certificate revocation list.fact: Publicly trusted CAs in the Web PKI are required (including by the CA/Browser forum) to issue CRLs for their certificates, and they widely do. Browsers and other relying parties might use CRLs, or might use alternate certificate revocation technologies (such as OCSP) or CRLSets (a dataset derived from CRLs) to check certificate revocation status.

Certificate revocation list.subject: Computer & IT
Certificate revocation list.question: Note that _____ is falling out of favor due to privacy and performance concerns, resulting in a return to CRLs
Certificate revocation list.fact: Browsers and other relying parties might use CRLs, or might use alternate certificate revocation technologies (such as OCSP) or CRLSets (a dataset derived from CRLs) to check certificate revocation status. Note that OCSP is falling out of favor due to privacy and performance concerns, resulting in a return to CRLs.

Certificate revocation list.subject: Computer & IT
Certificate revocation list.question: As a short-term fix, a patch was issued for the relevant _____ software (most importantly Windows) specifically listing the two certificates in question as "revoked"
Certificate revocation list.fact: In a noteworthy example, a certificate for Microsoft was mistakenly issued to an unknown individual, who had successfully posed as Microsoft to the CA contracted to maintain the ActiveX 'publisher certificate' system (VeriSign). Microsoft saw the need to patch their cryptography subsystem so it would check the status of certificates before trusting them.
